resources.string: A floating button that takes a screenshot, lets you mark it up and shares it.
FloatShot needs to display over other apps so its button can float on every screen. In the list that opens, pick FloatShot and turn on “Allow display over other apps”.
FloatShot can display over other apps.
If Android says it’s a restricted setting: open App info, tap ⋮ at the top right, choose “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Start it, then tap it on any screen to take a screenshot. The first time, Android asks you to allow screen capture. Tap “Start now”.
The button is on. Tap it on any screen to take a screenshot.
FloatShot is on. Tap the floating button on any screen.

On: screenshots are instant after you allow screen capture once. Android shows a screen-sharing icon while the button is on, and asks again after you lock your phone. Off: Android asks before every screenshot.
Tap the floating button to take a screenshot. It opens in the editor.
Mark it up with Pen, Marker, Arrow, Box and Text. Use Blur to hide private details and Crop to keep just the part you need.
Copy, Save or Share from the top bar. Saved screenshots go to Pictures/FloatShot in your gallery.
Drag the button to move it. Drag it onto ✕ at the bottom to turn it off.
Some phones close apps that run in the background. In App info, open Battery and choose “Unrestricted” or “Allow background activity”.
Your screenshots stay on your phone unless you share them. FloatShot has no internet access.
Couldn’t start the floating button. Try again.
Tap the floating button to take a screenshot.
Tap to edit and share it.
FloatShot is off. Open the app to turn it back on.
Allow FloatShot to display over other apps first.
Couldn’t take the screenshot. Try again.
FloatShot needs screen capture to take screenshots. Tap the button and choose “Start now”.
Copied. Paste it into any app.
